subject: Session pseudonymization & scheduled purge — post-call next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Aurelia Jacobs <aurelia.jacobs@medixcare.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Session pseudonymization & scheduled purge — post-call next steps

Hi Aurelia — great to meet today, thanks for the clear signal on risk appetite and constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope: 

What we heard (summary)
- PII (names, identifiers, contact details) must not be persisted in identifiable form in any Redwood-managed storage.
- MedixCare will accept short-lived operational artefacts for throughput reasons, provided the data is pseudonymized and purged within an agreed window.
- Data residency: all inference-related storage and logs must remain in EU regions and use customer-held encryption keys (KMS/HSM).
- Legal will want a purge SLA and an audit artifact (data flow diagram + SOC2 control mapping) before sign-off.

Redwood proposal (high-level)
- Pseudonymization: we can apply a one-way salt+hash to explicit PII at ingestion and keep the reversible mapping only under your KMS in a customer-only vault if required.
- Operational cache: propose a 72-hour session TTL for inference KV caches (masked indices only) with automated scheduled purge.
- PII retention: 0-retention for explicit PII fields — we will not persist those attributes in text logs or embeddings.
- Residency & keys: deploy POC in our EU region and bind encryption to your KMS key (supports HSM-backed keys).

Attachments: I attached a first-pass redline and a simple data flow diagram for the PoC (see attachments).

Requested next steps / asks
1) Can you confirm whether MedixCare requires reversible pseudonym mappings (i.e., ability to re-identify) or true irreversible hashing?
2) Will Legal accept a 72-hour masked-cache window for non-PII operational artifacts, or do they want a shorter window?
3) Please share any SOC2 or internal control sections Legal will reference so we can map evidence.
4) If acceptable, we propose a 30-day PoC with the TTLs above.

I can coordinate a brief (30min) legal + security sync next week to walk the redline. Priyom/Marissa — looping you for commercial/CS alignment.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0142

Attachment stubs: redwood-proposal-medixcare-ttl-redline.pdf (PDF, 3 pages) | session-data-flow.png (PNG, 1 image)

From: Aurelia Jacobs <aurelia.jacobs@medixcare.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: MedixCare Legal <legal@medixcare.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T20:45:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Session pseudonymization & scheduled purge — post-call next steps

Thanks Naomi — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side after an internal review: 

1) PII treatment: MedixCare policy prefers irreversible pseudonymization for PHI/PII by default. Reversible mappings are a last resort and will require a documented use-case and strict key control. If Redwood can do irreversible hashing with per-customer salts, that is preferable.

2) Operational cache window: our security lead will accept a short operational cache for performance but wants the following constraints: masks applied to indices (no raw text), TTL configurable down to 24 hours, and automatic purge jobs with logs we can audit.

3) Residency & keys: must be EU-only. Customer-managed keys are mandatory. We need proof that keys are not exported outside the EU.

4) Evidence: please provide a data flow diagram showing where PII is transformed, where masked indices live, and where audit logs are stored. A mapping to SOC2 CC6/CC7 controls (or equivalent) will speed Legal review.

5) SLA: we expect a contractual purge SLA that specifies maximum time-to-purge after a request or after TTL expiration. Legal will draft redlines if Redwood provides a sample clause.

We are open to a PoC but will prioritize the irreversible-pseudonymization-first approach. Proposed next step from our side: Legal can review Redwood's redline and we can schedule a joint security call early next week.

—Aurelia
Aurelia Jacobs
Head of Product Security, MedixCare
aurelia.jacobs@medixcare.com

Subject: RE: Session pseudonymization & scheduled purge — internal next steps

Naomi / Marissa — quick internal plan before we sync with Aurelia/Legal: 

1) Commercial: propose a 30-day PoC priced at $0, with standard rate card post-PoC. We should include an engineering time buffer for the per-customer TTL override and KMS binding work.

2) Security docs to prep: 
- Data flow diagram (we'll use the attached PNG and expand).
- SOC2 mapping doc (short table tying Redwood controls to common SOC2 criteria).
- Purge SLA sample clause (two options: 24h purge SLA / 72h purge SLA) — include both in the redline.

3) Engineering ask: eng team to confirm capability to enforce per-customer TTLs down to 24h and to provide an audit log of purge operations (timestamp + job id + hash footprint). If pseudonymization is irreversible, we need to confirm we can still support requested debug flows (we may need an opt-in reversible mapping under customer's KMS).

4) Ask Aurelia for a short prioritized list: {irreversible-only, irreversible with reversible-by-exception, reversible-by-default} so we can craft the redline accordingly.

I will draft the Purge SLA clause and push an initial redline to Naomi tonight. Marissa, can you confirm CS will run the PoC and provide an expected timeline for engineering onboarding?

Thanks,
Priyom
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Aurelia Jacobs <aurelia.jacobs@medixcare.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, MedixCare Legal <legal@medixcare.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Session pseudonymization & scheduled purge — redline + next steps

Aurelia — thanks for the clarity. Quick update and enclosed artifacts: 

What we attached
- redwood-proposal-medixcare-ttl-redline.pdf — contains two SLA clause options (24h purge / 72h purge), and language for irreversible pseudonymization with an optional reversible-by-exception flow that requires customer-controlled KMS unwrapping.
- session-data-flow.png — shows where PII is transformed (edge preprocess), where hashed indices live (masked KV store), and how purge jobs operate (queue -> worker -> audit log).

Key clarifications
- Irreversible hashing: we can do one-way salted hashes per-customer; salts are generated and stored only in your KMS if you want stronger isolation. This prevents Redwood staff from re-identifying by design.
- Reversible option: we support storing a reversible mapping but only if the key material is customer-held and the decryption operation is gatekept (requires a documented business justification and legal approval).
- Auditability: purge jobs generate an audit record (job id, timestamp, affected key-hash fingerprints). We can surface logs to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket in the EU for retention by MedixCare.

Proposed next steps
1) Please confirm preferred pseudonymization mode (irreversible vs reversible-by-exception).
2) Legal: if you can review the attached redline and mark any absolute blockers, we will incorporate and book the security sync.
3) If accepted, we will schedule a 60–90min kickoff to stand up the PoC in an EU region with the TTL configuration you prefer. Engineering estimate: 5–7 days of setup (including KMS binding).

If helpful I can join your Legal/Security call and walk through the redline clause language.

Best,
Naomi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
